slides.subtitle: What the estate census delivered, what remains open, and the evidence behind it
slides.title: Estate census close: accept a partial delivery, or hold

scqa: The census measured 638 of 1006 tables across 6 connections. It read 5.9m rows and 351.3 GiB of data and index in 15.5 minutes on the runtime.

Only 3 connections completed, 2 were partial and 1 was blocked: artists_app, access denied, grant pending. 44 tables failed, and 83 were stratified samples and 41 head samples. The counts by method do not sum to 638.
Should the owner accept the delivery and close the commission, or hold it open until the blocked connections are read?

Accept the delivery as a documented partial result, but hold the commission open. Closure should wait for the artists_app grant and re-census and for the failed tables to be re-run. Provenance is verified; completeness is not.
slides.title: The census is verified but partial; accept it as a record, not as closure

slides.title: Most measured tables had a complete pass, but sampling, failures and unreached tables remain

points: 638 of 1006 tables in scope were measured. That is usable evidence, but it is not an estate-wide census.
513 tables had a complete pass, the strongest basis. Ratios on these can be relied on for the tables concerned.
83 tables were measured by stratified sample and 41 by head sample. Their ratios are indicative only.
The three method counts do not sum exactly to 638. We disclose the difference and have not invented a residual category.
slides.title: 638 of 1006 tables were measured, with 513 by complete pass

points: 5.9m rows and 351.3 GiB of data and index were measured. These are measured quantities, not inferred ones.
259.3m rows held is an estimate of the estate's holdings. It must not be read as rows inspected.
44 tables failed because the worker could not measure them. Their contents are unknown until a re-census addresses the recorded errors.
The run took 15.5 minutes on the runtime. That is a duration only and should not be read as a cost.

points: 3 of 6 connections completed. 20 databases were measured across the estate.
2 connections, citizen_digital and citizen-pulse, are partial because some of their tables failed.
1 connection is blocked. artists_app returned an access denied error, the grant is pending, and no tables were reached.
Only the owner can grant that access. A re-census follows the grant.
Accepting the delivery does not remove these dependencies; they stay open either way.
slides.title: 3 of 6 connections are complete; 2 are partial and 1 is blocked

points: The ledger holds 3 rows for the run: admitted, warmed, then terminated successfully. This shows the run executed as governed.
The lawful basis admission is on file and covers the census only. The result receipt is digest-verified, which establishes provenance, not coverage.
The executive dossier used 17679 tokens in and 4583 tokens out. This is usage, not cost.
A separate enumeration reached 106 object storage buckets, and 40 were unreachable. It listed objects only and did not inspect their content.
slides.title: The run is traceable end to end, but traceability does not show completeness

points: Decide first: accept 638 of 1006 tables as a partial record, and hold closure. Acceptance does not remove the open items.
Grant access on artists_app, the one blocked connection, then commission a re-census.
Re-run the 44 failed tables once their recorded errors are addressed.
Run complete passes on the 83 sampled and 41 head-sampled tables where firm ratios matter.
Reconcile the method counts before quoting any coverage figure.
slides.title: Accept the partial record, but hold closure until blocked and failed tables are read

points: artists_app is unknown until the owner grants access and it is re-censused.
Ratios on the 83 stratified and 41 head-sampled tables are indicative only.
The 44 failed tables and the tables not reached are unmeasured.
Languages, rights and semantic similarity were not measured; rights need declaring at source.
Digest verification shows provenance, not completeness; closure needs the owner's explicit acceptance.
